CLINICAL FEATURES OF INFECTIVE ENDOCARDITIS
- Acute:
- High fever with rigors
- Delirium
- Shock
- Development of new murmurs
- Severe cardiac failure
- Abscesses may form in many parts of the body (e.g. brain)
- Subacute:
- Low-grade fever
- Signs of carditis
- Finger clubbing
- Arthralgia
- Splenomegaly
- Osler's nodules
- Janeway lesions
- Roth spots
